stem: Feed pH is within the intended range, but plants show persistent nutrient-availability symptoms and root-zone measurements differ from the feed. What is the best interpretation?
choices: Feed pH alone is not a complete diagnosis; root-zone chemistry and other evidence must also be evaluated
The correct feed pH proves root-zone conditions are correct
pH is unrelated to nutrient availability
Symptoms identify a single nutrient without other measurements
rationale: pH is chemical context, not a standalone diagnosis. Root-zone measurements and other evidence are needed when plant response does not match the feed reading.
